issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: SCB_EnableDCache(): Add check for already enabled DCache
Context: repo=STM32CubeF7, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-F767ZI, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=124
Root cause: Hi @aschlueter-dev, Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Set-up** * Board: NUCLEO-F767ZI * IDE/Compiler: SEGGER Embedded Studio 8.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-F767ZI, usage_question, high, enhancement, wontfix, spotted before customer, cmsis, IDE, SEGGER, core_cm7, SCB_EnableDCache, SCB

Technical details:
**Set-up** * Board: NUCLEO-F767ZI * IDE/Compiler: SEGGER Embedded Studio 8.24 / SEGGER Compiler **Description** In the file Drivers/CMSIS/Include/core_cm7.h, function SCB_EnableDCache(), the following code was added: c if (SCB->CCR & SCB_CCR_DC_Msk) return; /* return if DCache is already enabled */ This addition checks if the DCache is already enabled before proceeding with initialization. **Full function after change:** c /** \brief Enable D-Cache \details Turns on D-Cache */ __STATIC_INLINE void SCB_EnableDCache (void) { #if defined (__DCACHE_PRESENT) && (__DCACHE_PRESENT == 1U) uint32_t ccsidr; uint32_t sets; uint32_t ways; if (SCB->CCR & SCB_CCR_DC_Msk) return; /* return if DCache is already enabled */ SCB->CSSELR = 0U; /*(0U << 1U) | 0U;*/ /* Level 1 data cache */ __DSB(); ccsidr = SCB->CCSIDR; /* invalidate D-Cache */ sets = (uint32_t)(CCSIDR_SETS(ccsidr)); do { ways = (uint32_t)(CCSIDR_WAYS(ccsidr)); do { SCB->DCISW = (((sets << SCB_DCISW_SET_Pos) & SCB_DCISW_SET_Msk) | ((ways << SCB_DCISW_WAY_Pos) & SCB_DCISW_WAY_Msk) ); #if defined ( __CC_ARM ) __schedule_barrier(); #endif } while (ways-- != 0U); } while(sets-- != 0U); __DSB(); SCB->CCR |= (uint32_t)SCB_CCR_DC_Msk; /* enable D-Cache */ __DSB(); __ISB(); #endif } **How To Reproduce** 1. Call the function SCB_EnableDCache() when D-Cache is already enabled. 2. The new check will prevent re-initialization if DCache is already active. **Additional context** This change improves robustness by avoiding unnecessary initializations. The modification has been tested on the mentioned setup and works as intended.

Key comments:
Hi @aschlueter-dev, Thank you for this report. The change you are referring to is already present in the **STM32CubeH7** firmware, as you can see from [this](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/9a17eade6a3dce9d09530a0f74f5493d6a705fc3/Drivers/CMSIS/Include/core_cm7.h#L2332) line of code. Actually, the **STM32CubeF7** still supports an older version of the CMSIS Core interface, as you can see below: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/blob/ffc492ab7309b8dab6bf1b50b6d103863beb7a21/Drivers/CMSIS/Include/core_cm7.h#L2-L5 Please let me ask whether a migration to a newer version is planned. I will get back to you as soon as I have news. Hi @aschlueter-dev, Unfortunately, there is currently no plan to migrate to a newer version of the CMSIS Core interface, though it may be considered in the long term. Please allow me to close this issue. Thank you for your understanding.

issues.issue_title: UART DMA in IDLE Mode calls callback function twice in Half transfer
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: UART DMA in IDLE Mode calls callback function twice in Half transfer
Context: repo=STM32CubeF7, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F7XX, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=123
Root cause: Hello @Memarnejad, Thank you for the report.
Fix: Hi, **Describe the set-up** Develop a program in which UART Receive is in RX **IDLE** Mode Detection and uses **DMA** in **Circular** Mode for data transfer **Describe the bug** In the **middle** of transfer, HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback is called **twice**.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F7XX, HAL, DMA, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, uart, IDLE, HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback, HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA, ODD

Technical details:
Hi, **Describe the set-up** Develop a program in which UART Receive is in RX **IDLE** Mode Detection and uses **DMA** in **Circular** Mode for data transfer **Describe the bug** In the **middle** of transfer, HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback is called **twice**. once for _DMA half complete transfer_, another one for _IDLE_ detection. Although it's logical to detect both events, But I guess this It's not the intention of HAL developers, since callback is not called twice at the end of transfer (one for complete, another one for IDLE). So It's a bug base on this intention. **How To Reproduce** 1. Put UART reception in RX IDLE mode detection using HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() 2. Set the UART DMA in Circular Mode 3. Start Sending data to UART with gap in between to trigger IDLE Mode 4. if the transfer size is Even, the twice call is occured in exactly middle of transfer ((e.g. transferSize = 8; Problem occurs in 4th Byte, both half and idle events with 4 as Size parameter to HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback) 5. if the transfer size is ODD, the twice call is occured in ceiling of middle of transfer ((e.g. transferSize = 7; Problem occurs in 4th Byte, Half callback with 3 and Idle callback with 4 as Size parameter to HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback) **How to Fix** In stm32f7xx_hal_uart.c file, in HAL_UART_IRQHandler function, around line 2335, in IDLE line interrupt handling add another condition for circular mode: ((huart->hdmarx->Init.Mode != DMA_CIRCULAR) || (nb_remaining_rx_data != huart->RxXferSize / 2U)) to the below code: if ((huart->ReceptionType == HAL_UART_RECEPTION_TOIDLE) && ((isrflags & USART_ISR_IDLE) != 0U) && ((cr1its & USART_ISR_IDLE) != 0U)) { //Some Other Stuff.... //Some Other Stuff.... uint16_t nb_remaining_rx_data = (uint16_t) __HAL_DMA_GET_COUNTER(huart->hdmarx); if ((nb_remaining_rx_data > 0U) && (nb_remaining_rx_data < huart->RxXferSize) && ((huart->hdmarx->Init.Mode != DMA_CIRCULAR) || (nb_remaining_rx_data != huart->RxXferSize / 2U))) { //Some Other Stuff.... //Some Other Stuff.... } //Some Other Stuff.... //Some Other Stuff.... } The above Patch fixes the call of both IDLE event and Half Complete for transfer. Another problem is that when transfer size is ODD, half complete callback calls HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback with (somehow) wrong Size parameter (e.g. transferSize = 7; call back is called with floor(7/2) = 3, but this size was informed to callback in previous call to HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback with IDLE Event and ceil(7/2) = 4 MUST be informed now). To Fix this issue, in UART_DMARxHalfCplt function, use the ceil value: if (huart->ReceptionType == HAL_UART_RECEPTION_TOIDLE) { HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback(huart, ceil(huart->RxXferSize / 2.0)); } With above two patches, now for even transfer size, only half complete is called for transferSize / 2, and for odd transfer size, only half complete is called for ceil(transferSize / 2) Hope this fix helps others as well best regards

Root cause: See https://github.
Fix: The current implementation of the Ethernet driver appears to have been incorrectly copied from the H5/H7 HALs.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F7XX, HAL, ETH, bug_report, medium, bug, ETH_DMATXDESC_LS, ETH_DMATXDESC_TTSS, DESC0

The current implementation of the Ethernet driver appears to have been incorrectly copied from the H5/H7 HALs. These flags are from the DESC0 register, and the current implementation does not set the TX timestamp properly when required.

Technical details:
I've purchased a STM32F767ZI-Nucleo and found my way to this repository in an attempt to get one of the example projects up and running. I see that there's a [directory of projects for my particular board](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/tree/master/Projects/STM32F767ZI-Nucleo). However, what appears to be entirely missing are straightforward instructions on actually getting any of these up and running with any of the supported platforms. It seems like EWARM, MDK-ARM, and SW4STM32 are the most commonly supported, however oddly the STM32CubeIDE and STM32CubeMX makefile-style projects (which I'm familiar with) apparently aren't. This is odd given that those are ST products whereas the others I listed aren't. It also seems as though these example projects use the board's corresponding BSP, but don't themselves include it in their respective directories. I was able to find [this document](https://www.st.com/resource/en/user_manual/um2298-stm32cube-bsp-drivers-development-guidelines-stmicroelectronics.pdf) which details the layout of the BSPs, however it remains unclear precisely how to integrate that with any of the example projects. The only official documentation I can find on getting an example project up and running is the following (borderline humorous in its non-specificity and un-helpfulness) @par How to use it ? In order to make the program work, you must do the following: - Open your preferred toolchain - Rebuild all files and load your image into target memory - Run the application From my perspective, some basic documentation on how to get the project actually up and running on the physical board would be table stakes for a project like this. Surely the engineer who designed and built each project had to at least test it on the board itself using at least one of the supported toolchains -- could you not ask that person to document their project setup more precisely, so that your customers are able to straight-forwardly replicate their work and modify it for evaluation purposes?

Just open the .project file of an example of your choice using STM32CubeIDE and follow the instructions in the popup messages. A few clicks and you should be done. Actually, SW4STM32 is the "ancestor" of STM32CubeIDE, as both are based on Eclipse. @ALABSTM Thanks for the explanation. I did as described and the project appears to be building. Apologies for my pretentious tone, I was frustrated by my own ignorance. Hi @ibeckermayer, No worries. You're more than welcome.

Problem: HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() doesn't trigger IRQHandler() but manually enable RxDMA and IDLE IT works
Context: repo=STM32CubeF7, mcu_series=None, board=STM32H750VBTX, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=119
Root cause: This issue also happens on STM32H750VBTx.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * MCU: STM32F722RET6 * Complier: arm-none-eabi-gcc version 13.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32H750VBTX, HAL, DMA, bug_report, medium, bug, needs clarification, usart, MCU, STM32F722RET6, GNU, UART

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * MCU: STM32F722RET6 * Complier: arm-none-eabi-gcc version 13.2.1 20231009 (Arm GNU Toolchain 13.2.rel1 (Build arm-13.7)) * Debugger: GNU gdb (Arm GNU Toolchain 13.2.rel1 (Build arm-13.7)) 13.2.90.20231008-git **Describe the bug** If initialize the UART Rx DMA process using HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA(), we got **no USARTx_IRQHandler() triggered** (observed by setting a breakpoint) while **the related UART interrupt bit does occurs** in UART->ISR (IDLE/RXNE), and the UART->RDR remains the first byte we got, which causes another overrun flag. HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() returns HAL_OK, and the huart->hdmarx->State is HAL_DMA_STATE_READY, but the DMA Rx buffer still remain empty. **How To Reproduce** 1. CubeMX config: Rx DMA in Circular Mode, and got UART Global Interrupt and corresponding Rx DMA Interrupt enabled. 2. Configure the UART by HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() and receive data in HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback(), and compile+flash the program. 3. Send a series of bytes to UART which are shorter than Size passed to HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() 4. Even USARTx_IRQHandler() is untriggered, let alone HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback(). **Additional context** 1. First try to add a line after HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA(), but ends with the same problem: HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA(); __HAL_UART_ENABLE_IT(huart, UART_IT_IDLE); 2. Then I try to replace the HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() line with the following sequence, initializing the DMA process by directly modifying registers like what I have done in LL lib: // Initialize Rx DMA first WRITE_REG(huart->hdmarx->Instance->PAR, (uint32_t)&(huart->Instance->RDR)); // which equals to LL_DMA_SetPeriphAddress(); WRITE_REG(huart->hdmarx->Instance->M0AR, (uint32_t)rx_buffer); // LL_DMA_SetMemoryAddress(); MODIFY_REG(huart->hdmarx->Instance->NDTR, DMA_SxNDT, rx_size); // LL_DMA_SetDataLength(); ATOMIC_SET_BIT(huart->Instance->CR3, USART_CR3_DMAR); // LL_USART_EnableDMAReq_RX(); SET_BIT(huart->hdmarx->Instance->CR, DMA_SxCR_EN); // LL_DMA_EnableStream(); // then, to be compatible with HAL_UART_IRQHandler() logic, I added some extra lines: huart->pRxBuffPtr = rx_buffer; huart->RxXferSize = rx_size; huart->ReceptionType = HAL_UART_RECEPTION_TOIDLE; huart->RxEventType = HAL_UART_RXEVENT_TC; // finally, enable UART __HAL_UART_ENABLE_IT(huart, UART_IT_IDLE); __HAL_UART_ENABLE(huart); Then, I got everything work as expected. But one thing weird to me is that the sequence above should do mainly the same as HAL function, so I hadn't figured out where's the problem inside HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() function.

This issue also happens on STM32H750VBTx. I tried optimize level from -Os to -O3 with same result, and the solution is most likely the same, just replace huart->hdmarx->Instance with ((DMA_Stream_TypeDef*)huart->hdmarx->Instance) because the type of DMA_HandleTypeDef.Instance in stm32h7xx_hal_dma.h is void*. In RM0410, for STM32F76xxx and and STM32F77 xxx boundary of SRAM2 is from 0x2007 C000 to 0x2007 FFFF. In description of Flash register, OPTCR1 in details we read: BOOT_ADD1[15:0]: Boot base address when Boot pin =1 BOOT_ADD1[15:0] correspond to address [29:14], The boot memory address can be programmed to any address in the range 0x0000 0000 to 0x2004 FFFF with a granularity of 16KB. Example: BOOT_ADD1 = 0x0000: Boot from ITCM RAM (0x0000 0000) BOOT_ADD1 = 0x0040: Boot from System memory bootloader (0x0010 0000) BOOT_ADD1 = 0x0080: Boot from Flash on ITCM interface (0x0020 0000) BOOT_ADD1 = 0x2000: Boot from Flash on AXIM interface (0x0800 0000) BOOT_ADD1 = 0x8000: Boot from DTCM RAM (0x2000 0000) BOOT_ADD1 = 0x8004: Boot from SRAM1 (0x2002 0000) BOOT_ADD1 = 0x8013: Boot from SRAM2 (0x2004 C000) This description is wrong because address 0x2004 FFFF is boundary for SRAM2 on stm32f75 and 74 series. Following row sets full frame length as buffer length: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/blob/6a3b9bb8d09839f365ba83a6cf5823ae5f5226db/Drivers/STM32F7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_eth.c#L1129 This causes RxDataLength to be incorrect as it is just incremented by buffer length: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/blob/6a3b9bb8d09839f365ba83a6cf5823ae5f5226db/Drivers/STM32F7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_eth.c#L1150 The same buffLength is also given to rxLinkCallback as parameter instead of size of the latest buffer.

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 152028 @Maashau First of all thanks for sharing your input in public, so user can find it and get informed before a fix from ST is made available. Did investigate to understand your bug report and wanted to share my results, as on a first look i was not understanding what happens. I did assume that buffer size does mean ETH_RX_BUF_SIZE. The issue (at my point of view) seems to be that the size of the last chunk on chained buffers (why it shouldn't matter when buffer size is equal or bigger then ethernet frame) is calculated wrong. This is the case because the FL / ETH_DMARXDESC_FL part of the RDES0 / DESC0 part returns the whole frame length including the CRC. Sentence from ref manual for this: _"These bits indicate the byte length of the received frame that was transferred to host memory (including CRC)."_ So it seems that there was a misunderstanding that this part of the register does return the buffer byte count or it was not foreseen that the ETH_RX_BUF_SIZE is smaller than ethernet frame size. To my limited understanding of the ethernet hardware / code, the right bufflength should be easily calculated by subtracting of the already received bytes

issues.issue_title: __LL_TIM_CALC_PSC rounding
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: __LL_TIM_CALC_PSC rounding
Context: repo=STM32CubeF7, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=LL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=57
Root cause: Hi @phryniszak, Thank you for your report.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** /** * @brief HELPER macro calculating the prescaler value to achieve the required counter clock frequency.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, bug_report, medium, bug, good first issue, internal bug tracker, hal, HELPER, Min_Data, Max_Data

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** /** * @brief HELPER macro calculating the prescaler value to achieve the required counter clock frequency. * @note ex: @ref __LL_TIM_CALC_PSC (80000000, 1000000); * @param __TIMCLK__ timer input clock frequency (in Hz) * @param __CNTCLK__ counter clock frequency (in Hz) * @retval Prescaler value (between Min_Data=0 and Max_Data=65535) */ #define __LL_TIM_CALC_PSC(__TIMCLK__, __CNTCLK__) \ (((__TIMCLK__) >= (__CNTCLK__)) ? (uint32_t)(((__TIMCLK__)/(__CNTCLK__)) - 1U) : 0U) Works as expected when the result of division is integer, but in the other case result is truncated, not round. So in my case when I call it with values: __LL_TIM_CALC_PSC(108*1e6, 10*1e6); function returns precaller value 9 which gives counter frequency 10.8*1e6 (8% error). Better value is 10 with counter frequency equal 9.8*1e6 (2% error). I didn't check but it looks like this macro is present in most of stm32cube packages in the same form. **Additional context** https://www.google.com/search?q=Rounding+integer+division

Key comments:
Hi @phryniszak, Thank you for your report. Indeed, the issue is confirmed. To fix it you can use the patch below : diff /** * @brief HELPER macro calculating the prescaler value to achieve the required counter clock frequency. * @note ex: @ref __LL_TIM_CALC_PSC (80000000, 1000000); * @param __TIMCLK__ timer input clock frequency (in Hz) * @param __CNTCLK__ counter clock frequency (in Hz) * @retval Prescaler value (between Min_Data=0 and Max_Data=65535) */ #define __LL_TIM_CALC_PSC(__TIMCLK__, __CNTCLK__) \ - (((__TIMCLK__) >= (__CNTCLK__)) ? (uint32_t)(((__TIMCLK__)/(__CNTCLK__)) - 1U) : 0U) + (((__TIMCLK__) >= (__CNTCLK__)) ? (uint32_t)((((__TIMCLK__) + (__CNTCLK__)/2U)/(__CNTCLK__)) - 1U) : 0U) The fix will be made available in the frame of a future release. ST Internal Reference: 118234 Hi @phryniszak, Thank you for your contribution. This issue has been fixed in the frame of version v1.17.0 of the STM32CubeF7. Please allow me then to close this thread. Thank you again for your contribution.

Keywords: STM32F7XX, HAL, DMA, high, duplicate, STM32F769I-DISCO, IDE, FATFS, SD_FindSCR, SD_HandleTypeDef, SDMMC_FLAG_RXOVERR, SDMMC_FLAG_DCRCFAIL

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** The board is STM32F769I-DISCO. The IDE is OpenSTM32. Using CubeMX 5.3.0 with FreeRTOS with FATFS and SD card DMA template. HAL version is 1.16.1. **Describe the bug** The bug appears from time-to time as the system falling into Hard Fault for no apparent reason. In the file **stm32f7xx_hal_sd.c** there is a function static uint32_t SD_FindSCR(SD_HandleTypeDef *hsd, uint32_t *pSCR) which has the followng code: while(!__HAL_SD_GET_FLAG(hsd, SDMMC_FLAG_RXOVERR | SDMMC_FLAG_DCRCFAIL | SDMMC_FLAG_DTIMEOUT | SDMMC_FLAG_DBCKEND)) { if(__HAL_SD_GET_FLAG(hsd, SDMMC_FLAG_RXDAVL)) { *(tempscr + index) = SDMMC_ReadFIFO(hsd->Instance); index++; } if((HAL_GetTick() - tickstart) >= SDMMC_DATATIMEOUT) { return HAL_SD_ERROR_TIMEOUT; } } Please note that *(tempscr + index) may overflow as tempscr is only two elements long and the loop never checks for an array boundary. Also, there are two more places worth fixing for buffer overrun which use SDMMC_ReadFIFO(hsd->Instance) in the same file. But they are not used in the DMA template. Pull request created: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/pull/55

Problem: Wrong prescaler value in HAL_InitTick() when Timer clocks less than 1MHz
Context: repo=STM32CubeF7, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F746ZGT6, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=configuration_help, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=35
Root cause: Hi @stsymbaliuk, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: TIM7 selected as Timebase Source HCLK in Clock config set to 1 MHz APB1 Prescaler is 4 APB1 Timer clocks: 0.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F746ZGT6, HAL, configuration_help, high, cube mx, TIM7, HCLK, APB1, MCU, HAL_InitTick, HAL_RCC_GetPCLK1Freq

Technical details:
TIM7 selected as Timebase Source HCLK in Clock config set to 1 MHz APB1 Prescaler is 4 APB1 Timer clocks: 0.5 MHz MCU: STM32F746ZGT6 STM32CubeMX Version 6.1.0 STM32CubeF7 Firmware Package V1.16.0 / 14-February-2020 Observed behavior looks like uwTick does not change but in fact due to very high prescaler it counts very slow. File stm32f7xx_hal_timebase_tim.c, HAL_InitTick() function c /* Compute TIM7 clock */ uwTimclock = 2*HAL_RCC_GetPCLK1Freq(); // 2 * 250000 = 500000 /* Compute the prescaler value to have TIM7 counter clock equal to 1MHz */ uwPrescalerValue = (uint32_t) ((uwTimclock / 1000000U) - 1U); // (500000U / 1000000U) - 1U = 0 - 1U = 4294967295 (max uint32_t value) So for uwTimclock less than 1 million uwPrescalerValue must be 0 and not 4294967295. Quick and dirty fix is to replace line c uwPrescalerValue = (uint32_t) ((uwTimclock / 1000000U) - 1U); with c uint32_t mhz = (uwTimclock / 1000000U); if (mhz > 1) { uwPrescalerValue = mhz - 1; } else { uwPrescalerValue = 0; } And line c htim7.Init.Period = (1000000U / 1000U) - 1U; can be replaced with c if (mhz > 1) { htim7.Init.Period = (1000000U / 1000U) - 1U; } else { htim7.Init.Period = (uwTimclock / 1000U) - 1U; } Or if such Timer clocks unsupported by CubeMX some error message can be displayed ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44534615/100466970-6f1b5c80-30da-11eb-8367-a4c3dcfc6fed.png)

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: USBD_LL_GetRxDataSize/HAL_PCD_EP_GetRxCount return wrong value
Context: repo=STM32CubeF7, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F7XX, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=30
Root cause: Hi @davekeck, Thank you for this clear and concise report and for the fix proposal.
Fix: When both of these conditions are true: - A USB OTG HS device has DMA enabled ("Enable internal IP DMA" checkbox in the UI) - USBD_LL_PrepareReceive is used to initiate a transfer that's larger than the max packet size Under these circumstances, when the DataOut USB callback is called as a result of USBD_LL_PrepareRece
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F7XX, HAL, USB, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, OTG, DMA, USBD_LL_PrepareReceive, USBD_LL_GetRxDataSize, HAL_PCD_EP_GetRxCount

Technical details:
When both of these conditions are true: - A USB OTG HS device has DMA enabled ("Enable internal IP DMA" checkbox in the UI) - USBD_LL_PrepareReceive is used to initiate a transfer that's larger than the max packet size Under these circumstances, when the DataOut USB callback is called as a result of USBD_LL_PrepareReceive, USBD_LL_GetRxDataSize/HAL_PCD_EP_GetRxCount return an incorrect value for the number of bytes received. The bug appears to be due to these lines in PCD_EP_OutXfrComplete_int: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/blob/08376dce1b404687e4a86b73077f396bccfc9cb5/Drivers/STM32F7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_pcd.c#L1986-L1990 Th above math incorrectly uses the the max packet size (instead of the transfer size), so that when the transfer size is larger than the max packet size, xfer_count is assigned to an incorrect value, which breaks USBD_LL_GetRxDataSize/HAL_PCD_EP_GetRxCount. This replacement code fixes the issue for me: c const uint32_t xfer_len = hpcd->OUT_ep[epnum].xfer_len; const uint32_t xfrsiz = (USBx_OUTEP(epnum)->DOEPTSIZ & USB_OTG_DOEPTSIZ_XFRSIZ); if (xfer_len) { const uint32_t xfer_count = xfer_len - xfrsiz; hpcd->OUT_ep[epnum].xfer_count = xfer_count; hpcd->OUT_ep[epnum].xfer_buff += xfer_count; } else { hpcd->OUT_ep[epnum].xfer_count = 0; }

Key comments:
Hi @davekeck, Thank you for this clear and concise report and for the fix proposal. It has been forwarded to our development teams. I will get to you as soon as they provide their feedback. ST Internal Reference: 120891

**Describe the bug** The macro __HAL_RCC_USB_OTG_FS_CLK_ENABLE https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/blob/08376dce1b404687e4a86b73077f396bccfc9cb5/Drivers/STM32F7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32f7xx_hal_rcc_ex.h#L845-L852 declares the local variable tmpreg and calls the macro __HAL_RCC_SYSCFG_CLK_ENABLE which is defined as https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF7/blob/08376dce1b404687e4a86b73077f396bccfc9cb5/Drivers/STM32F7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32f7xx_hal_rcc.h#L468-L474 and also declares a local variable with the name tmpreg. I suggest the rename tmpreg in __HAL_RCC_USB_OTG_FS_CLK_ENABLE to something else. **How To Reproduce** Use __HAL_RCC_SYSCFG_CLK_ENABLE() somewhere in the source with the compiler flag -Wshadow set.

The STM32F74 reference manual is not clear on the relationship between the status flags for the DPSM and the FIFO and I have understood from the reference manual that the DBCKEND flag can be set when the FIFO still contains data that has not been read. If that is the case then the existing code will not work correctly when the processor is slowed down ( through low clock speed or interrupt load ). The HAL_SD_ReadBlocks() function uses the SDMMC_FLAG_DATAEND flag rather than SDMMC_FLAG_DBCKEND and then continues to empty the FIFO. SD_SendSDStatus() seems to have similar code to SD_FindSCR but it continues to empty the FIFO after the DBCKEND flag. **How To Reproduce** 2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...). stm32f7xx_hal_sd.c : SD_FindSCR() 3. The use case that generates the problem. I have not been able to confirm my suspicions here. 4. How we can reproduce the problem. **Additional context** My fix for this is to test for SDMMC_FLAG_DBCKEND only after SDMMC_FLAG_RXDAVL has been fully serviced: while(!__HAL_SD_GET_FLAG(hsd, SDMMC_FLAG_RXOVERR | SDMMC_FLAG_DCRCFAIL | SDMMC_FLAG_DTIMEOUT )) { while(__HAL_SD_GET_FLAG(hsd, SDMMC_FLAG_RXDAVL)) { tempscr[index++] = SDMMC_ReadFIFO(hsd->Instance); } if (__HAL_SD_GET_FLAG(hsd, SDMMC_FLAG_DBCKEND) && !__HAL_SD_GET_FLAG(hsd, SDMMC_FLAG_RXDAVL)) { // end of data transfer from Card and from FIFO break; } if((HAL_GetTick() - tickstart) >= SDMMC_DATATIMEOUT) { return HAL_SD_ERROR_TIMEOUT; } } I think that the non-interrupt data read function should be factored out of the three routines ( SD_SendSDStatus, SD_FindSCR, HAL_SD_ReadBlocks ).

Root cause: The workaround is to either: - disable DCache using SCB_DisableDCache(); or by not enabling it in the first place - not use DMA in USB Host Working, however not the best solution is to: - Enable DMA by changing hhcd.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * STM32F746G-DISCO * STM32F7xx HAL Drivers V1.

Keywords: STM32H750, HAL, USB, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, internal bug tracker, st community, projects, STM32F746G-DISCO, STM32

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * STM32F746G-DISCO * STM32F7xx HAL Drivers V1.2.7 * STM32 USB Host Library V3.3.2 * gcc 6.3.0 from TouchGFX 4.12.3 toolchain * Modified USB Host configuration USB_Host/MSC_RTOS/Src/usbh_conf.c to contain hhcd.Init.dma_enable = 1; instead of hhcd.Init.dma_enable = 0; **Additional context** In my project I have FreeRTOS, STM32 USB Host Library and FatFs. The FatFs driver and Host Library configuration files are taken from MSC_RTOS example. The example does not use DMA and I wanted to enable it. I thought I could just change the flag dma_enable to 1 but it doesn't work unless I disable DCache. I have captured the raw USB traffic using OpenVizsla USB analyzer. It is apparent that the SETUP transactions do not contain valid data (zeros only; however the CRC is correctly calculated for all zeros) when the configuration is changed to contain hhcd.Init.dma_enable = 1; and the main() contains SCB_EnableDCache();. For example, the very first SETUP transaction sent to device when DMA is not used is: USB Packet (2d 00 10) PID: SETUP (0x2d) [Source: host] [Destination: 0.0] .... .... .000 0000 = Address: 0 .... .000 0... .... = Endpoint: 0 0001 0... .... .... = CRC5: 0x02 [correct] [CRC5 Status: Good] USB Packet (c3 80 06 00 01 00 00 08 00 eb 94) PID: DATA0 (0xc3) Data: 8006000100000800 CRC: 0x94eb [correct] [CRC Status: Good] USB Packet (d2) PID: ACK (0xd2) to such request the device replies correctly wih the 8 bytes of the Device Descriptor, and the rest of enumeration and the actual FatFs driver works fine. USB Packet (69 00 10) PID: IN (0x69) [Source: host] [Destination: 0.0] .... .... .000 0000 = Address: 0 .... .000 0... .... = Endpoint: 0 0001 0... .... .... = CRC5: 0x02 [correct] [CRC5 Status: Good] USB Packet (4b 12 01 10 02 00 00 00 40 55 41) PID: DATA1 (0x4b) Data: 1201100200000040 CRC: 0x4155 [correct] [CRC Status: Good] USB Packet (d2) PID: ACK (0xd2) However when the SCB_EnableDCache(); is called during initialization and DMA is enabled in usbh_conf.c, the very first SETUP transaction sent to device is malformed: USB Packet (2d 00 10) PID: SETUP (0x2d) [Source: host] [Destination: 0.0] .... .... .000 0000 = Address: 0 .... .000 0... .... = Endpoint: 0 0001 0... .... .... = CRC5: 0x02 [correct] [CRC5 Status: Good] USB Packet (c3 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 bf f4) PID: DATA0 (0xc3) Data: 0000000000000000 CRC: 0xf4bf [correct] [CRC Status: Good] USB Packet (d2) PID: ACK (0xd2) and the device (obviously) STALLs when host tries to read data: USB Packet (69 00 10) PID: IN (0x69) [Source: host] [Destination: 0.0] .... .... .000 0000 = Address: 0 .... .000 0... .... = Endpoint: 0 0001 0... .... .... = CRC5: 0x02 [correct] [CRC5 Status: Good] USB Packet (1e) PID: STALL (0x1e)

Key comments:
The workaround is to either: - disable DCache using SCB_DisableDCache(); or by not enabling it in the first place - not use DMA in USB Host Working, however not the best solution is to: - Enable DMA by changing hhcd.Init.dma_enable = 0; to hhcd.Init.dma_enable = 1; - Force Write-Through before enabling DCache: SCB->CACR |= SCB_CACR_FORCEWT_Msk; - Invalidate DCache inside HAL_HCD_HC_NotifyURBChange_Callback(): SCB_InvalidateDCache(); That way, the changes are solely in user code, i.e. in the usbh_conf.c and the place where SCB_EnableDCache(); is called. A better solution would be to ensure cache coherency at the STM32 Library level. Hi Desowin, Welcome back! Thank you for this detailed description of the behavior you observed. He will take in charge analyzing this issue and the solutions you suggested. > Force Write-Through before enabling DCache Just a warning: I believe the STM32F746NG is affected by the general Cortex-M7 errata regarding write-through cache (spurious data loaded after a sequence of loads and stores).
